item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
That's fair enough. I don't disagree with you and can see why you may say what you're saying.

My only rebuttal to this is that the situation the kid and the agent are in is a bit strange in a few ways. First, the Kid is a little… disenfranchised at this point. He's fairly resigned to his fate and is more frustrated with telling the story than he is upset. He gets upset at certain points, but overall it's supposed to be more of a tone of frustration.

As for the agent, he's purposely being very dry and calm. He's pretending to be the kid's defense attorney and doesn't want anything to really compromise that. It's also a fairly effective interview technique to keep your mouth shut and let the subject talk as much as possible, which is what the agent did here.

Perhaps I could have worked out the roommate's personality more, but I didn't think it was particularly important here past his connection to the college kid.

Okay, I'm just getting defensive now, I apologize. Maybe this will help you understand why I have him talking like it's another day in the park.

I should also mention that I did have another version of the interview where I had him much more emotional. I had a lot of critique of it being fairly over the top. To each their own, I guess.

If I get some time in the future I'll try to massage this a bit to make it a bit more personable. :) Thanks for the critique!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The ritual was sufficiently weird to be interesting and I liked the horror of the room-mate self-dissassembling, but the dialogue from the college kid was, frankly, pretty bad. I couldn't picture a terrified or frustrated college student talking like that. It didn't help that the Foundation agent was cardboard bland, which made the kid's dialogue stand out even more, with nothing to play against. I also didn't get much sense of the kid's dead roommate's personality other than he was apparently into "some weird shit" in a way that made him want to try one of the rituals… I guess?

Oh, and college kids like video games. Carmen Sandiego was a huge hit of nostalgia, so props for that.

Finally, this entry doesn't seem to do much to support its parent article. If it'd been in the parent article, it would have been enough for me to downvote. You can get the box to the Foundation without having to wade through this interrogation.
